title: The Group Project Disaster
summary: Four classmates nearly ruin their group project by waiting until the night before it is due, but they stay calm, divide the work fairly, and finish together just in time.
poll: It is fine to wait until the last minute on a group project, as long as everyone works hard the night before it is due.

versions.title: The Group Project
versions.text:
Omar, Huda, Yusuf, and Noor are in Grade 6. They have a class project. It is about the water cycle.

The project is due in one day. But no one has started. Each one thought the others would do the job.

At last, the four friends meet. They see that nothing is done. No notes. No poster.

"Stop!" says Huda. "Let's stay calm. We can make a plan."

They look at what is left. They split up the jobs. Omar will draw. Yusuf will write. Noor will find facts.

They all work hard that night. Step by step, they finish the poster.

They finish just in time! The next day, they do a great job. Now they know: talk and plan at the start, not at the end.

keyWords.definition: a piece of work done over time, often for school
keyWords.example: Our class project about plants took two weeks to finish.

keyWords.definition: to decide ahead of time what you will do
keyWords.example: We need to plan our trip before Friday.

keyWords.definition: to complete something, so there is nothing left to do
keyWords.example: She finished her homework before dinner.

keyWords.definition: quiet and not worried or upset
keyWords.example: He stayed calm even when the test was hard.

keyWords.definition: a task that someone is given to do
keyWords.example: Cleaning the board is my job this week.

questions.stem: What is this story mostly about?
options: Four friends learn how to swim together at the school pool, then win a prize
Four friends plan a class trip to the beach, then forget to bring any food
Four friends almost fail a project because they never planned, then fix it together
Four friends compete to get the best grade alone, then lose the contest and quit
questions.why: The story follows Omar, Huda, Yusuf, and Noor as they almost fail their project from not planning, then come together to finish it in time.

wrong.A: There is no swimming in the story.
wrong.B: No beach trip is mentioned.
wrong.D: They work together, not alone, and do not compete against each other.

questions.stem: What is the class project about?
options: The water cycle
The history of Jeddah
How to bake bread
Famous Saudi artists
questions.why: In the story, the group project is about the water cycle.

wrong.B: The story does not mention the history of Jeddah as the topic.
wrong.C: Baking is never mentioned.
wrong.D: Artists are not the topic of this project.

questions.stem: Why is nothing done when the friends finally meet?
options: The teacher took their notes away
Each one thought someone else would do the job
They lost their project at school
They worked on the wrong project by mistake
questions.why: The story explains that each friend assumed someone else would handle the work, so nobody actually did it.

wrong.A: The teacher never takes anything away in the story.
wrong.C: Nothing is described as lost.
wrong.D: They are working on the right project; they just have not started.

questions.stem: What happens right after the friends see that nothing is finished?
options: They decide to quit the project
They call their teacher for help
They go home without talking
For a moment, they feel worried
questions.why: The story says that for a moment, everyone felt worried, right after they discovered nothing was done.

wrong.A: They do not quit; they make a plan instead.
wrong.B: They do not call the teacher in the story.
wrong.C: They stay and talk; they do not go home.

questions.stem: Why does Huda tell everyone to stay calm?
options: So they do not waste time panicking and can make a plan instead
Because the teacher told her to say it before the class began
Because she wants to go home early and finish the work later
Because the project is already finished and nothing more is needed
questions.why: Huda wants the group to stop panicking so they can use the time left to plan and finish the work.

wrong.B: No teacher gives her this instruction in the story.
wrong.C: Going home early is never mentioned.
wrong.D: The project is not finished; that is the whole problem.

questions.stem: How do the friends most likely feel when they see nothing is done?
options: Proud and relaxed
Worried and surprised
Bored and sleepy
Angry at their teacher
questions.why: Since the project is due soon and nothing is ready, the friends would naturally feel worried and surprised.

wrong.A: Nothing suggests they feel proud or relaxed at this point.
wrong.C: Discovering a crisis is unlikely to feel boring.
wrong.D: The story never says they are angry at their teacher.

questions.stem: In the story, the word calm means —
options: fast and full of energy and fun
angry and loud and upset
quiet and not worried or upset
tired and ready for bed
questions.why: Huda asks everyone to stay calm, meaning quiet and not worried, instead of panicking.

wrong.A: Calm is not about speed or energy.
wrong.B: Calm means the opposite of angry and loud.
wrong.D: Calm does not mean tired.

questions.stem: Why does the author show that nothing is finished the night before it is due?
options: To explain how posters are made by students
To describe the water cycle in detail, with rain
To show that Huda is the smartest student here
To show why it is bad to wait and not plan early
questions.why: Showing the group's panic the night before the deadline teaches the lesson that waiting too long to plan causes problems.

wrong.A: The story is not a guide to making posters.
wrong.B: The water cycle facts are not explained in detail here.
wrong.C: The story is not about ranking who is smartest.

The school was closed for two weeks because of rain
Each one assumed someone else would handle the job
They did not have the right materials at home
questions.why: The story explains that each friend simply assumed someone else would take care of the work, so nobody started.

wrong.A: The teacher did assign and explain the project.
wrong.B: The school being closed is never mentioned.
wrong.D: Missing materials are not given as a reason in the story.

questions.stem: Why does everyone begin to panic when they meet online?
options: They realize how little time is left to finish an unstarted project
They forgot the name of their project and cannot find their notes
Their teacher cancels the project, so they have no work to do
They cannot find the water cycle poster board in the class
questions.why: Discovering that almost nothing is done the night before the deadline naturally causes panic about the little time remaining.

wrong.B: Forgetting the project's name is never mentioned.
wrong.C: The teacher does not cancel the project.
wrong.D: A missing poster board is not the issue; the poster simply has not been made yet.

questions.stem: Why does Huda's calm response help the group?
options: It gives the others someone to blame for the mess
It makes the project due later than the teacher said
It finishes the poster for everyone in the class
It stops the panic and gets everyone focused on a plan
questions.why: By staying calm, Huda helps the group stop panicking and start making a clear plan to finish the work.

wrong.A: Huda is not blaming anyone in the story.
wrong.B: The deadline does not change.
wrong.C: Huda's words do not finish the poster by themselves; the group still has to do the work.

questions.stem: In the story, the word divide means —
options: to draw a picture of something
to split something into separate parts
to finish an entire job quickly without any help at all
to feel worried about a deadline
questions.why: The friends divide up the remaining jobs, meaning they split the work into separate parts for each person.

wrong.A: Divide is not about drawing.
wrong.C: Divide is not the same as finishing quickly.
wrong.D: Divide does not describe a feeling.

questions.stem: How does the author organize the story?
options: By comparing two different schools
By listing facts about Jeddah
By showing a problem, then how the friends solve it together
By explaining how the water cycle works, step by step
questions.why: The story first shows the problem of nothing being finished, then shows how the friends calmly solve it together.

wrong.A: Only one school is described.
wrong.B: Jeddah facts are not listed in the story.
wrong.D: The water cycle itself is not explained step by step; it is only the topic of the project.

MID.prompt: Explain what went wrong with the group's planning, and how the four friends fixed the problem. Use at least two details from the story.
checklist: I explained what went wrong with the planning.
I explained how the friends fixed the problem.
I used at least two details from the story.
MID.modelAnswer: The group's planning went wrong because each friend assumed someone else would do the work, so nobody started the project for almost two weeks. When they finally met the night before it was due, nothing was finished. They fixed the problem by staying calm instead of panicking, and by dividing the remaining jobs fairly based on what each person was good at, which let them finish just in time.

keyWords.definition: to delay doing something that needs to be done
keyWords.example: If you procrastinate on your science project, you will be rushing at the last minute.

keyWords.definition: to give part of a job to someone else to do
keyWords.example: The team captain delegated one task to each player.

keyWords.definition: to work together with others to create or finish something
keyWords.example: The two artists collaborated on a mural for the school wall.

keyWords.definition: being responsible for your own actions or tasks
keyWords.example: Taking accountability means admitting your part when something goes wrong.

keyWords.definition: to share information or ideas with someone else
keyWords.example: Good teammates communicate early so no one is confused about the plan.

questions.stem: Which statement best expresses the central idea of the story?
options: Waiting until the last minute to divide work can nearly cause a group project to fail, but clear communication can still save it.
Group projects about the water cycle are more interesting than other topics.
Teachers should never give students more than one night for a project.
Noor is, without any doubt whatsoever, unquestionably and by far the single most talented and capable member of the entire four-person group.
questions.why: The story shows how procrastination and a lack of clear roles nearly caused the project to fail, and how communicating and delegating fairly saved it just in time.

wrong.B: The story does not compare the water cycle to other topics.
wrong.C: The problem was not the amount of time given, but how the friends used it.
wrong.D: The story does not rank the friends by talent; each contributes in a different way.

questions.stem: According to the story, what had the friends failed to do during the two weeks before the deadline?
options: Choose and carefully select an appropriate topic for their group project
Explicitly agree on who was responsible for each part
Tell their teacher about the project
Find a poster board to use
questions.why: In the story, nobody had ever explicitly agreed on who was responsible for which specific component.

wrong.A: The topic, the water cycle, was already assigned by the teacher.
wrong.C: The teacher already knew about and assigned the project.
wrong.D: A missing poster board is never given as the problem.

questions.stem: What can you infer caused the friends to procrastinate for almost two weeks?
options: The teacher forgot to assign the project
The friends were waiting for new art supplies
Each one assumed someone else would take care of it
They did not understand the water cycle at all
questions.why: In the story, each friend individually assumed someone else would eventually handle the work, which explains the delay.

wrong.A: The teacher did assign the project at the start.
wrong.B: Art supplies are never mentioned as a reason for the delay.
wrong.D: A lack of understanding of the water cycle is never given as the cause.

questions.stem: Why does Huda's suggestion to communicate clearly help solve the group's problem?
options: It convinces the teacher to extend the deadline for the whole class
It finishes the research for them automatically, without any more work
It makes the project due the following week instead of that day
It allows them to divide the remaining work and avoid wasting time on panic
questions.why: Clear communication lets the group quickly agree on who does what, so they can use the limited remaining time efficiently instead of panicking.

wrong.A: The deadline is never extended in the story.
wrong.B: Communicating does not do the research for them; they still have to do the work.
wrong.C: The due date does not change.

questions.stem: Based on the story, why might delegating tasks according to each person's strengths have helped the group finish on time?
options: Each person could work faster and better on a task suited to their skill
It meant only one person had to do any work at all, so the others rested
It guaranteed the teacher would give them a perfect grade on the project
It allowed them to skip checking their facts, so they saved time
questions.why: Assigning Omar to drawing, Yusuf to writing, and Noor to checking facts let each person work efficiently on what they were best at, saving precious time.

wrong.B: All four friends work that night, not just one person.
wrong.C: No grade is mentioned as guaranteed in the story.
wrong.D: Noor's job is specifically to check the facts carefully, not skip that step.

questions.stem: In the story, the word accountability means —
options: a drawing tool used for posters and for school projects
being responsible for your own actions or tasks
a kind of school deadline for a group's work
the number of people in a group at the school
questions.why: The friends realize nobody had taken accountability, meaning nobody had taken responsibility for a clearly defined task.

wrong.A: Accountability is not a drawing tool.
wrong.C: Accountability is not a type of deadline.
wrong.D: Accountability does not refer to a group's size.

questions.stem: In what order did these events happen?
options: The poster is finished, the friends panic, Huda speaks up
Huda speaks up, the friends panic, the poster is finished
The friends panic, Huda speaks up, the poster is finished
The poster is finished, Huda speaks up, the friends panic
questions.why: The friends first panic upon discovering nothing is done, then Huda speaks up to calm everyone and suggest a plan, and only afterward is the poster finished.

wrong.A: The poster could not be finished before the panic happens; panic comes first.
wrong.B: Huda speaks up after the panic begins, not before it.
wrong.D: The poster is finished last, after Huda speaks up, not before the panic.

questions.stem: Why does the author end the story with the friends reflecting on what went wrong?
options: To suggest that group projects should be banned from school, since they cause arguments
To show that Omar's drawing was the real problem, because it was poor and late
To explain exactly how the water cycle works, with rain, rivers and the sea
To emphasize the lesson that early communication prevents last-minute crises
questions.why: The closing reflection highlights that the real issue was a lack of early communication, driving home the story's lesson for readers.

wrong.A: The story does not argue against group projects in general.
wrong.B: Omar's drawing is never blamed; the issue was the lack of a plan.
wrong.C: The water cycle's science is not the focus of the ending.

HIGH.prompt: Do you agree that communicating and planning early could have completely prevented the group's problem? Support your argument with evidence from the story, and address a counterargument.
checklist: I supported my position with specific evidence from the story.
I addressed at least one point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I agree that communicating and planning early could have prevented almost all of the group's problem. The story shows that the real cause of the crisis was not the project's difficulty, but the fact that nobody had explicitly agreed on who was responsible for each part during the two weeks they had. If the friends had delegated tasks on the first day, as they eventually did the night before the deadline, they would not have needed to panic at all. Someone might argue that procrastination is simply common among students and cannot always be prevented, but the story shows that a short, calm conversation was all it took to fix the problem once the friends finally communicated clearly.

LOW.stem: Which job does Omar take in the group?
options: He finds facts
He writes the notes
He talks to the teacher
He draws
LOW.why: In the story, Omar's job is to draw.

wrong.A: Noor is the one who finds facts.
wrong.B: Yusuf is the one who writes.
wrong.C: Talking to the teacher is not a job in the story.

LOW.stem: The text says the project is due the next day. What does due mean?
options: It must be finished in one day
It will be a lot of fun for one day
It was started one day ago
It is too hard for one day
LOW.why: No one has started and the project is due in one day, so they have only one day to finish.

wrong.B: The text does not say it is fun.
wrong.C: No one has started the project.
wrong.D: They finish it in time, so it was not too hard.

LOW.stem: What lesson do the friends learn at the end?
options: Drawing is better than writing
Teachers like long projects
Talk and plan at the start
Work alone to go faster
LOW.why: The last lines say they know to talk and plan at the start, not at the end.

wrong.A: The friends need both drawing and writing.
wrong.B: The text does not say what teachers like.
wrong.D: They finished by working as a team.

LOW.stem: What do the friends do right after they split up the jobs?
options: They go home to sleep
They work hard that night
They give the project to a teacher
They start a new project
LOW.why: In the story, they all work hard that night.

wrong.A: They stay up to finish the poster.
wrong.C: They give it to the teacher the next day, after it is finished.
wrong.D: They finish this project; they do not start another.

MID.stem: Where did the four friends meet to check on their progress?
options: In the school library
At Omar's house
Online
On the school bus
MID.why: The text says the four friends met online on the night before the deadline.

wrong.A: The library is not mentioned.
wrong.B: Omar's house is not mentioned.
wrong.D: The bus is not mentioned.

MID.stem: In the story, the word "assumed" in "each one simply assumed" means —
options: knew for sure
forgot about
refused to believe
thought without checking
MID.why: Each friend thought another would do the job, without checking, and no one did it.

wrong.A: They were wrong, so they did not know for sure.
wrong.B: They thought about it, so they did not forget.
wrong.C: The word is about what they thought, not refusing to believe.

MID.stem: Why did Omar agree to draw the poster?
options: He was the best artist
He had finished the facts
He lived near the school
He was the oldest friend
MID.why: The text says Omar agreed to draw because he was the best artist.

wrong.B: No facts were finished yet.
wrong.C: Where he lived is never mentioned.
wrong.D: His age is never mentioned.

MID.stem: What does "with only minutes to spare" show about the friends' work?
options: They finished a week early
They gave up before the end
They almost ran out of time
They worked very slowly
MID.why: Having only minutes to spare means they finished just before time ran out.

wrong.A: Minutes to spare is not a week early.
wrong.B: They finished the poster.
wrong.D: They worked hard that night and finished.

HIGH.stem: Why was Noor chosen to double check the facts?
options: She did not want to draw
She was meticulous and detailed
She had the most free time
She was the group's teacher
HIGH.why: In the text, Noor was meticulous and detailed, so she checked that every fact was accurate.

wrong.A: Her wish to draw is not mentioned.
wrong.C: Free time is not mentioned.
wrong.D: She is a student, not a teacher.

HIGH.stem: In the story, the word "procrastinate" most nearly means —
options: to put off doing a task
to finish a task very early
to share a task fairly
to check a task twice
HIGH.why: Nobody started for almost two weeks because each friend assumed someone else would do it.

wrong.B: They finished at the last moment, not early.
wrong.C: They shared the jobs only on the last night.
wrong.D: They did not check anything until the end.

HIGH.stem: What was missing when the friends met online?
options: The teacher's help and a computer
A topic and a due date
A group leader and a map
Notes, facts, and a poster
HIGH.why: The text says there were no written notes, no researched facts, and no poster whatsoever.

wrong.A: They met online, so they had a computer, and the teacher is not mentioned.
wrong.B: They knew the topic and the deadline.
wrong.C: A map is not mentioned, and Huda took the lead later.

HIGH.stem: Why does the author end with what the friends realized about the real problem?
options: To show that the teacher was unfair to them
To show the poster was poor
To show they should work alone
To share a lesson about planning early
HIGH.why: The ending says the problem was that no one took a clear job, so now they plan and talk at the start.

wrong.A: The teacher praised their teamwork.
wrong.B: They did an excellent job presenting.
wrong.C: The lesson is about working together better, not alone.
